answer: Each identity tends a public hash spiral that must be extended at irregular times listed in a shared prism of upcoming slots. Every extension is a signed, one-time sonnet line: a short unique payload that cannot be reused or handed to another name. Miss a slot, or let two names extend in the same instant from one operator, and the chain is burned. Because one operator can keep only a few spirals alive through a tight, staggered schedule, a farm of idle copies goes dark and carries no weight.
